# HRP Rule 3 - Follow high-roleplay escalation This standard tightens [textlink="Roleplay Rule 11 - Follow reasonable escalation" link="RuleR11"] for high roleplay. All of Rule 11 still applies; the points below raise the bar.
- Conflict must be built through roleplay. Reach for words, then social or non-harmful pressure, long before violence. (Unless you're a antagonist then this may change.) - Do not skip escalation steps. Match the other party's level, but do not jump ahead of it. - Attempt to de-escalate where it is reasonable. Someone watching your whole round should never conclude that your goal was to find a fight. - You need a clear in-character reason for [color=#ff0000]lethal force[/color]. "They annoyed me" or "they were in my way" is not enough for a non-antagonist. - The permanently-lethal stage should almost never be reached, and only when the other party brought the conflict there.
Antagonists remain exempt from escalation as described in Rule 11, but are still expected to build their conflicts with roleplay rather than opening with immediate maximum violence.
## Examples Acceptable: - A dispute over a workspace starts with an argument, then a shove, then a fistfight, each step a response to the other person. - As security, you talk to a suspect first, warn them, then use non-lethals when they resist. - As an antagonist, you manipulate and pressure a target over several minutes before your plan turns violent.
Prohibited: - Pulling a weapon and going lethal over a verbal insult. - "Winning" a minor argument by immediately critting the other person. - Treating every round as an excuse to start fights and hunt for conflict. - As an antagonist, gibbing a random bystander at roundstart for no roleplay reason.
